headline: Test 1: Portugal, 1441–1486 · 31:46

items.title: 31:46 · To scale high-mortality plantation and maritime extraction
items.detail: To scale high-mortality plantation and maritime extraction, the Portuguese Elite needed a labor supply stripped of domestic legal standing and severed from local kin networks.

items.title: 31:56 · Two older institutional templates were already available
items.detail: Two older institutional templates were already available in the Mediterranean archive for the Portuguese Crown to adapt.

items.title: 32:03 · Chapter 8 documents the older internal template
items.detail: Chapter 8 documents the older internal template: the legal subjugation of European women through feudal coverture and the targeted destruction of female reproductive and healing autonomy during the witch trials.

items.title: 32:15 · Chapter 3 documents the external commercial template
items.detail: Chapter 3 documents the external commercial template: the centuries-old trans-Saharan and Mediterranean slave routes, where captives of Slavic, Circassian, Berber, and sub-Saharan African origin were traded alongside shifting religious rationales including early adaptations of the Curse of Ham.
